finding.before: The native request “Make only the roof chrome and keep its red paint color” did not receive E's exactPart claim. Parent routing selected a Chrome Cross Colors decorative candidate, adding a new roof pattern layer and changing paint/spec across seven zones. Owner Undo removed the unintended edit.
finding.repair: Added an anchored whitelist for same-part preserve-current-paint/color tails. The preceding phrase must already parse as exactly one known named-part finish-only action with one look and no color, relative adjustment, extra action, unknown words, or leftovers. The tail is removed only from the planner input after that proof; the plan does not assign a color.
finding.after: Native phrase now plans one exact roof operation with chrome look and null color. Thus the existing finish-only reuse path can preserve the current red paint and existing zone identity.
finding.safety: Cross-part preservation remains a protected-parts ask. Mixed recolor/preserve, texture/pattern additions, multiple targets, questions, negatives, whole-car requests and unknown parts do not become exactPart plans.

results: Existing named-part command contract passed (12 simple plans, 6 non-claims, 3 unknown/material guards, 3 preservation/composition guards)

limitations: This verifies E.plan only; it does not verify live proAI precedence, current owner/provenance, queue, paint/spec output or Undo. Root owns the native integration rerun.

The alternate imperative “Apply a chrome finish only to the roof, preserving its existing red color” remains unsupported because its base command is not accepted by the existing parser; the preserve-tail repair does not broaden command grammar.

The named color in a preservation tail is not emitted as an assignment or compared with zone pixels here. Parent must retain existing unique-current-owner gating and the finish-only reuse path that preserves the current zone color.
